walkthroughs.body_html:
Formulae, Equations & Amounts — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Formulae, Equations & Amounts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Formulae, Equations & Amounts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which species has the same electron configuration as Ar?
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
F⁻
Mg²⁺

mcqs.q: Successive ionisation energies of an atom always:
options: Decrease
Stay the same
Increase
Vary randomly

mcqs.q: How does a fuel cell differ from a conventional battery?
options: Fuel cells and batteries are identical — both just store electrical energy.
A fuel cell continuously consumes externally supplied fuel (e.g. hydrogen) and oxidant; a battery has a fixed amount of reactants that get used up.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
Fuel cells burn fuel to generate heat which is then converted to electricity.

mcqs.q: Why does the colour of a transition metal complex change when ligands are exchanged?
options: Different ligands cause different amounts of d-orbital splitting, so different wavelengths of light are absorbed.
The colour changes because the metal ion itself changes oxidation state.
The colour changes because the new ligand is itself coloured.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.

mcqs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
options: Graphite conducts because it is a metal, while diamond is a non-metal.
Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond has all four outer electrons in localised covalent bonds.
Fuel cells burn fuel to generate heat which is then converted to electricity.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
